findings.title: Invalidate cache status after deleting cached data
findings.body: The delete-cache mutation only invokes the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates connectedCalendars. The wrapper forwards an optional onChanged callback and disables refetchOnWindowFocus, so deleting the cache can leave the old timestamp and delete action displayed after the success toast. Invalidate viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars after deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does, so the displayed status reflects the database.

findings.title: Resolve persisted cache records for delegated calendar connections
findings.body: Connected calendars can use in-memory delegation credentials with negative IDs, while CalendarCache rows belong to persisted credentials. getCachedAvailability explicitly supports this by looking up delegated availability using userId and key, including reusing an existing OAuth connection's cache after delegation is enabled. This new credential-ID-only lookup cannot find those same rows, so cacheUpdatedAt becomes null and the dropdown hides both status and deletion for the delegated connection even while its cached availability is being served. Resolve the user's persisted cache credentials for these connections and use an ownership-checked deletion path for them.

findings.title: An empty Prisma update does not refresh updatedAt
findings.body: updateManyByCredentialId forwards this empty object directly to Prisma. Prisma does not bump an @updatedAt field when the update data is empty, so this call leaves SelectedCalendar.updatedAt unchanged after every cache refresh instead of recording the refresh time as intended. Supply updatedAt explicitly, or remove this unused timestamp-tracking call if CalendarCache.updatedAt is the sole freshness marker.

findings.title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script
findings.body: ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's working directory, not the script's location. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore creates or modifies .env in the repository's parent directory, leaving the application's environment unchanged while reporting success. Derive the repository root from the script's location before selecting the environment file.

findings.title: Make the environment update work with GNU sed
findings.body: The sed -i '' invocation uses BSD/macOS syntax and fails with GNU sed. On Linux, once GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, rerunning this helper leaves the old URL in place but still prints that it was updated successfully. Subsequent Google Calendar watches consequently use the stale tunnel endpoint. Use a portable replacement strategy or handle both sed variants, and check the command's exit status before reporting success.
